subject: Private offer: approval triggers for multi-division buyers & term tradeoffs
messages:
From: Harper Johnson <harper.j@finovate.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@finovate.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer: multi-division signoff & term questions

Diego — thanks for the demo this morning. We’re excited about Redwood but need to understand how a private offer would work across our three business units. Procurement here has asked:

- Which approvals trigger at corporate (CFO/legal) vs BU level?
- Can term length differ per BU if we want a consolidated PO?
- What evidence do you need for activation (SOC/SLA/usage forecast)?

Right now the ask from procurement is: have a joint plan for approvals and a draft PO they can circulate to their CFOs. Can you share an approach and timeline?

Best,
Harper
Harper Johnson
Head of Partnerships, Finovate Analytics
harper.j@finovate.com

From: diego.fernandez@redwood.com <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Harper Johnson <harper.j@finovate.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer: multi-division signoff & term questions

Harper — thanks for the clear list. We can definitely support a consolidated private offer and have a few common patterns that fit multi-BU customers. High level: 

1) Approval gates: for purchases that will be billed from a single PO but consumed by multiple BUs, AWS typically requires a corporate-level signature (legal/finance) for the PO itself and BU-level approvers for budget signoff. We usually map the external approver list in the PO to the BU finance leads.

2) Term flexibility: AWS private offers are activated against a single offer record. Term length per BU can be modeled inside a commercial SOW or MSA (e.g., staggered start/true-up windows), but the Marketplace contract/offer itself should have a canonical term to simplify activation. If BUs need different durations, we suggest a base 12-month offer with BU-level SOWs that specify usage or extendability.

3) Evidence for activation: SOC2 report, security questionnaire answers, a short usage forecast (3-mo ramp + 12-mo expected), and a named admin list. I’ll attach a draft PO and an evidence checklist.

I’m looping in Neha (marketplace ops) and Vanessa (seller lead) to confirm activation steps and any AWS-side gating. Proposed timeline: we produce a draft PO + evidence pack by Fri (9/17) so procurement can circulate to CFOs next week. Does that work?

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
Diego: (415) 555-0187

From: neha.kapoor@redwood.com <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com, harper.j@finovate.com
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer: multi-division signoff & term questions

Hi all — quick ops notes from the marketplace side (copying the checklist I’ll attach):

- AWS gating: buyer must be eligible on marketplace and have a linked AWS account per BU. If the buyer wants one consolidated invoice, they should confirm a single paying account and whether inter-BU chargebacks are internal to them.
- Offer record: the private offer metadata (price, unit, term) is single-valued. If you need differing BU pricing, we can set up usage-based SKU splits and map SKUs to BU units, but that complicates invoicing.
- Approvals: Procurement -> BU finance (approval for spend) -> Corporate signoff (legal/PO). For large strategic deals we request an internal approver list in the HubSpot deal to speed activation.

Attachments: I’ve uploaded a draft PO template (Finovate_PO_Draft_20270915.pdf) and an evidence pack template (Finovate_Evidence_Pack.zip). Also adding standard language we request in the MSA for staggered BU commitments.

Operationally: if Finovate wants different term windows, the simplest path is: create a 12-mo base private offer, then separate BU SOWs that reference the offer (SOW can include ramping/early termination clauses). If legal at Finovate insists on 24-mo for one BU, we can discuss a commercial credit to align the offer term.

I’ll coordinate with AWS activation team once we have the signed PO + evidence pack.

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
Marketplace GTM, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: diego.fernandez@redwood.com, harper.j@finovate.com
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2027 13:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer: multi-division signoff & term questions

Harper / Diego — adding a few commercial and cadence suggestions from seller ops and channel: 

- Recommended path: 1) get corporate procurement to confirm the paying account and internal chargeback method; 2) share the draft PO and evidence pack with the three BU CFOs simultaneously (we’ll provide a 1-page exec summary per BU); 3) request a 72-hour window for comments then finalize.
- Pricing concession: if Finovate signs a consolidated 24-mo commitment across any two BUs we can offer a modest unit discount (5-8%) but it requires VP-level approve on our side.
- Activation window: AWS activation typically takes 3-5 business days after we submit the signed private offer + evidence. If procurement needs immediate start dates per BU, we can backdate invoicing but that must be spelled out in the PO/SOW.

DocuSign link (for later): https://www.docusign.net/sign/Finovate-PO-4938
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/4938

Vanessa Ortiz

Harper — attaching the files Neha prepared and a short runbook for your procurement team. Next steps we recommend: 

1) Procurement confirms paying account and sends a list of BU approvers by Mon (9/20).
2) We’ll finalize and share the drafted private offer + SOWs by Tue (9/21).
3) Finovate returns the signed DocuSign by Fri (9/24) to target activation the week of 9/27 (AWS 3-5 business day window).

If any of the BU CFOs want a longer term for their BU, note that the marketplace offer must stay canonical; we’ll work with legal on a credit/compensation structure. Happy to jump on a 30-min call with the procurement and one BU CFO to walk through the flow — suggest Tue 9/21 10:00am PT.

Thanks and talk soon,
Diego
